Your AI agents are only as good as the content infrastructure behind them. Most enterprises have not caught up.

A new report from Box confirms what many CTOs suspect: AI agents have entered mainstream enterprise deployment, but the content management layer — the unstructured data, documents, and knowledge repositories these agents depend on — remains fragmented, siloed, and unprepared.

This gap is about to become the primary bottleneck for enterprise AI performance. Consider the scale: Google reported processing 3.2 quadrillion tokens per month at I/O 2026, up fiftyfold year-over-year. Gemini now has over 900 million monthly active users. Google also introduced Gemini Spark, a persistent background AI agent.

The implication is clear. AI agent adoption is accelerating at platform scale. But when these agents cannot access, interpret, or act on enterprise content reliably, they produce hallucinations, incomplete outputs, and workflow failures. The model is not the weak link. The data layer is.

For CEOs, this reframes the AI investment priority. The next dollar spent should not go toward a more powerful model. It should go toward content architecture — making your organization's knowledge accessible, structured, and agent-ready.
